Interaction studies

Two references.
Two interactions.

Independent reconstructions isolating the two interaction principles behind InBudget’s Three.js PBR lodge stage and privacy-preserving group shortlist.

01 / Staged product disclosure

From one hero stay to the full lineup.

Hold the active quote in focus while supporting options fan apart cleanly so the group never loses its visual anchor.

03 · Laurel Lodge$179.00
02 · Ridge House$142.00
01 · Fern Hollow$110.01

Deconstruction. One focal object, staged disclosure, stable visual anchor. On the home screen, scrolling smoothly pulls the Three.js camera from a hero close-up into a three-island lineup while keeping the selected stay, per-night share, and verdict synchronized.

02 / Live state attribution

See exactly what changed.

Select a layer, then adjust finishes or group size while the stay card and per-person split update in place.

Canopy roof · Spruce

Ridge House4 Travelers
$142.00$47.33 / night · Fits everyone

Deconstruction. Explicit part selection and immediate visual feedback make state transitions effortless to attribute. InBudget applies the same immediate feedback across the 3D diorama, plaque bar, price spectrum track, and budget slider.

How the studies became InBudget

Spatial continuity. The intro fly-in, 360° auto-orbiting Three.js PBR dioramas, plaque selector, and shortlist price track all address the same three stays in the same order, so clicking an island in 3D, pressing arrow keys on the plaques, or tapping a stop on the price track updates every view together.

Privacy-first group math. Each traveler enters or slides their private cap on their own device; the round stores and reveals only unanimous stay fit and the shared budget band—never anyone’s individual limit.
